name: Dollar Tree, Inc.
reason: Mid-transformation after the Family Dollar divestiture and multi-price rollout, with EPS 5y CAGR of only 0.4%, EPS at 0.8x its 2022 peak and 10y ROIC averaging 5.6%; the go-forward earnings base is not yet forecastable.

name: Healthpeak Properties, Inc.
reason: FFO/share has shrunk at -5.3%/yr over 10y (3.16 to 1.84) with share count up 4.2%/yr, net debt/EBITDA 6.1x and lab-space oversupply; no route to 7% growth.

name: DocuSign, Inc.
reason: E-signature is maturing (consensus EPS growth slowing to ~10%) and faces AI/platform disintermediation, while adjusted EPS runs ~289% above GAAP so the high FCF yield is inflated by stock-based compensation.

name: Dover Corp.
reason: A good but not special diversified industrial: 10y revenue CAGR only 1.5% with acquisitions at 0.68x FCF, and EPS at its 10y peak with EBIT margin at a 10y high of 17.9%, so the 10% EPS CAGR leaned on M&A, margin and buybacks.

name: Dow, Inc.
reason: Commodity petrochemicals with EPS swinging from 8.98 (2021) to a -0.94 loss (2025), EBIT margin 0.8% and net debt/EBITDA 4.85x; earnings are set by feedstock and polyethylene spreads.

name: Domino's Pizza, Inc.
reason: Asset-light global franchisor with 10y EPS CAGR 17.3%, 8/10 years of >=7% growth, ROIC ~71%, stable 16.5-19.3% EBIT margins and steady unit growth plus buybacks; 4.4x securitized leverage is acceptable for a defensive franchise royalty stream.

name: DTE Energy Co.
reason: Regulated Michigan utility with 6.0% 10y EPS CAGR, persistently negative FCF and net debt/EBITDA 6.6x; regulator-set returns and no special edge.

name: Duke Energy Corp.
reason: Regulated utility with 3.3% 10y EPS CAGR (1/10 years >=7%), negative FCF and net debt/EBITDA 6.1x; ordinary and capital-hungry.

name: DoubleVerify Holdings, Inc.
reason: Ad-verification duopoly with IAS but GAAP EPS has fallen to 0.30 from 0.41 in 2023 as walled gardens and pricing pressure squeeze margins (EBIT 10.8% vs 22% peak); acquisitions at 0.63x FCF and no adjusted EPS history.

name: EchoStar Corp.
reason: Binary transformation via spectrum sales after a -50.41 EPS loss in 2025 and net debt/EBITDA 18.6x; the residual business and capital deployment cannot be forecast.

name: Consolidated Edison, Inc.
reason: Regulated NY utility with 3.4% 10y EPS CAGR, negative FCF and net debt/EBITDA 5.1x; no route to 7% growth.

name: Equifax, Inc.
reason: Bureau oligopoly but 10y EPS CAGR only 5.4% (1.9% over 5y) with acquisitions at 1.13x cumulative FCF, earnings tied to mortgage originations and regulatory/pricing risk to Workforce Solutions; consensus 15-19% growth depends on a mortgage recovery.

name: Enphase Energy, Inc.
reason: Residential solar is policy-driven (25D credit expiry, NEM changes) and highly competitive: EPS at 0.64x its 2022 peak and consensus FY1 EPS -33%.

name: Enerpac Tool Group Corp.
reason: Small cyclical tools business with 10y revenue CAGR of -6.8% (divestitures) and 10y EPS CAGR of 0.9%; EBIT margin is at a 10y high of 22.6% and EPS at its peak.

name: EPR Properties
reason: Experiential REIT concentrated in movie theaters, FFO/share (5.12) still below 2018's 6.10, net debt/EBITDA 5.6x and consensus FFO growth ~0-4%; a cheap but structurally challenged tenant base.

name: Essential Properties Realty Trust, Inc.
reason: Net-lease REIT whose FFO growth comes from acquiring properties funded with external equity and debt (net debt/EBITDA 4.6x, negative FCF after acquisitions); consensus growth ~2% and no moat.

name: EQT Corp.
reason: Natural gas producer whose earnings follow Henry Hub prices (EBIT margin swung from -30% to 64%); growth came via acquisitions (1.31x FCF) and shares rising 14.9%/yr.

name: Element Solutions, Inc.
reason: Electronics/specialty chemistry with flat 10y revenue (0.0% CAGR), M&A at 0.51x FCF, margin at the 91st percentile and adjusted EPS ~90% above GAAP; the AI-packaging upside in consensus (17-22%) is cyclical and hard to underwrite.

name: Essex Property Trust, Inc.
reason: Well-run West Coast apartment REIT, but FFO/share CAGR is 5.0% over 10y (3/10 years >=7%) with net debt/EBITDA 5.5x; no route to 7% growth.

name: Etsy, Inc.
reason: Marketplace GMS has been shrinking under Temu/Shein/Amazon competition, with EPS at 0.41x its 2021 peak, 5y EPS CAGR -12.4% and net debt/EBITDA 3.1x; FCF is real but the franchise is eroding.
